body: Thanks for taking the time for reporting this, we appreciate it a lot :)

I'm happy to help. I was unaware that the 3.0.0 release was so soon. I had earmarked CakePHP for review and hoped to look at it before it got released in case something like this was lurking within the source. (Better to have BC-breaking changes on a major release than a minor one, after all.)

Life and work both got in the way of my plans. I apologize for that.
We will look into implementing the changes that don't involve BC breaks as soon as possible. We are evaluating already your recommendations

We can probably do the hash_equals change pretty easily - even including your polyfill shouldn't be bc incompatible in a patch release.

As far as the cbc issue, what would be the simplest fix for our codebase? Replacing with another library would be good, but seems like a heavyweight solution. Not sure how we'd handle that specifically re: semver releases though.

> As far as the cbc issue, what would be the simplest fix for our codebase?

I'm not sure. I could go through the trouble of providing a lengthy pull request to ensure all ciphertexts are authenticated, but the BC breaks would be severe and I would get an enormous -1 from security industry experts who, rightfully, believe there are already enough crypto libraries to clean up after and we don't need any more.

There are other issues I'm discovering that make securing the framework seem like an increasingly daunting task.

`Text::uuid()`, for example, would benefit greatly from https://github.com/ircmaxell/RandomLib as the current implementation uses `mt_rand()` and is not suitable for security contexts (e.g. `Security::generateAuthKey()`).

I'm sorry to say it, but your best bet might be to just provide shims to the implementations invented elsewhere and retag the 3.0.0 release. Unless you're comfortable jumping straight to 4.0.0 over these issues.
What ever path you decide to take, please let me know if you need my assistance.

`Security::generateAuthKey()` isn't even used, so we can remove that. I don't think there is an issue with any other usages of `Text::uuid()`. I've made a pr to remove the `generateAuthKey` method.

If you'd like, we'd appreciate an email - security@cakephp.org - with any findings and your recommendations so that we can fix what we think are critical and create work arounds for cases which aren't as trivial. We definitely appreciate your work so far.

Okay, I'll do just that. As I alluded to earlier in my OP (from the wrong account, heh), I'm in the middle of a lot of activities right now. It might be a few days before I can get to it. If I forget to do it, please feel free to send me an email or tweet to remind me.
- https://twitter.com/voodooKobra
- scott@arciszewski.me

issue.body: Based on the feedback in #6139 this implements a more time safe comparison for HMACs and recommends not using `Text::uuid()` for crypto use cases.

body: The timing side channel has been corrected (as much as it can be). The CBC-byte flipping is less of a burning concern as the Mcrypt/OpenSsl adapters are not intended to be used directly and the `Security::encrypt()/decrypt()` interface always includes an HMAC.
Instead of using `strlen()` in your `_constantEquals()`, I recommend using something like the `safeStrlen()` in https://github.com/symfony/symfony/pull/14028/files
Is that to work around the mbstring overloading of str functions?
